title: UK balance of payments, Jul-Sep 2026 (ONS, 07:00 London / 02:00 ET) — the Q3 current account, which in twelve years has never once published without GDP beside it
source: EST: ons.gov.uk/releases/balanceofpaymentsukjulytoseptember2026, re-fetched direct 2026-09-10 (HTTP 200, 42,105 bytes) — the ONS release page reads verbatim 'Balance of payments, UK: July to September 2026', 'Release date: 22 December 2026 7:00am', 'This release is not yet published', summary 'A measure of cross-border transactions between the UK and rest of the world. Includes trade, income, capital transfers and foreign assets and liabilities', with the Office for Statistics Regulation accredited-official-statistics statement on the release page itself. Cadence corroborated from the publisher's own search index (api.beta.ons.gov.uk, fetched direct 2026-09-10, HTTP 200): 47 balance-of-payments bulletins from 2014-12-23 to 2026-06-30, the Q3 edition printing on 20-23 December in all twelve years 2014-2025. Filed estimate on this lane's no-self-confirm limit and because market-events-data.ts's confirmed-prefix taxonomy has no slot for the UK Office for National Statistics; the date is the publisher's own and is not in doubt
notes: CANONICAL FILE WRITTEN BY THE never-assessed INITIAL RESEARCH OF THIS EVENT, 2026-09-10, after reading the single prior proposal (from-uk-public-sector-finances-2026-12-22) in full. The proposal's date, time and cadence evidence all reproduce. Its ONE claim that does not is the ranking it assigned this release inside the 07:00 stack — 'the clearest sterling channel of the five'. Measured, that claim is not merely unsupported, it is UNTESTABLE ON THIS CALENDAR: the ONS balance-of-payments and GDP-quarterly-national-accounts release-date series are IDENTICAL, 47 of 47 dates, 2014-12-23 through 2026-06-30, zero exceptions — the current account has never once published without GDP beside it, and the annual Pink Book has never published without the Blue Book beside it. So the 0.77x/0.81x/0.75x 'QNA release day' readings the sibling lane cited are the same 47 sessions as a 'BoP release day', not a comparable sample, and no release-day study can ever apportion a 07:00 move between GDP and the current account. Re-measured first-party here on those 47 days: IGLT.L 0.76x an ordinary day (t = -2.10), GBP/USD 0.81x (t = -1.75), US 10y 0.76x (t = -2.34), FTSE 1.00x — sterling QUIETER, not more active, which is the opposite direction from the proposal's ranking. Second amendment: this is NOT a re-benchmarking print. The September QNA states its own basis verbatim — 'this release contains data that are consistent with the UK National Accounts, the Blue Book 2025, which will be released on 31 October 2025' — so the annual benchmark lands at the SEPTEMBER print (2026-09-30 here, D-20), and the October Pink Book is documentation of a re-basing already published. Tiered LOW and symbols [] on that measured basis and because this repo tracks no UK-listed name and no house playbook is fiscal-, rates- or sterling-keyed. Estimate widens caution only; nothing date-keyed may act on this.
